title: Nelliyampathy & Munnar Back-Door Loop
tagline: Bangalore → Coimbatore → Palakkad → Nenmara → Pothundi dam → Nelliyampathy → Pollachi → Udumalpet → Chinnar → Marayoor → Munnar → Anachal glass bridge → Bodimettu ghat → Theni → Dindigul → Salem → Bangalore. ~1,260 km over four days, entering and leaving Munnar by its two quiet roads.
summary: Two Kerala hill stations from the reels, joined by the roads nobody uses. Nelliyampathy first — the underrated one, a 15 km ghat above Pothundi dam that ends at the Seetharkundu cliff and the forest department's jeep tracks. Then instead of the Kochi highway, Munnar from the back: Udumalpet through Chinnar sanctuary to Marayoor's sandalwood forest and up the Kanthalloor side. The Anachal glass bridge — shut on its opening day in Dec 2025 and reopened by court order in July 2026 — is 12 km out of Munnar; after it, the reel says, 'the real thrill begins': the steep estate road below Anachal. Leave Munnar east over the Bodimettu ghat into Tamil Nadu and run home through Theni and Dindigul.

credit.name: @sherry_thegirlnextdoor (Nelliyampathy) & @the_pretty_escape.travel (Munnar glass bridge) on Instagram
credit.note: two reels; the back roads between them are the point of this loop

segments.note: Day 1: the highway day. Six lanes all the way; Coimbatore for the night.
Day 2. Through the Palakkad gap into Kerala.
Nenmara is the last town: fuel and food — nothing past here on the hill.
15 km of ghat with 10-plus hairpins through forest, then estates to the top. Seetharkundu viewpoint is a short path off the road; Kaikatty forest IB books the jeep tracks.
Back down and across the state line on the quiet Kollengode road. Night 2 in Pollachi.
The back door: a forest road through Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary (check post, daytime only), then Marayoor's sandalwood reserve and Kanthalloor's orchards.
Climb through Eravikulam's fringe to Munnar. Night 3 in Munnar.
Day 4. The glass bridge is at Kanachery above Anachal — 35 m long, 40 people at a time. The estate road below it is the steep, tight bit from the reel.

segments.road: Anachal → Munnar → Bodimettu ghat → Bodinayakanur → Theni
segments.note: Out the east side: the Bodimettu ghat drops from 1,500 m to the Tamil Nadu plains in 30 km of forest hairpins — Munnar's best-kept road.
Home; 425 km on day 4, so start Anachal early.

highlights: Seetharkundu — the cliff-edge viewpoint at Nelliyampathy, 1,000 ft straight down to the Palakkad plains, usually with a waterfall in view.
Nelliyampathy's forest jeep tracks to Mampara — wild elephants at dawn, bookable at Kaikatty (₹50 entry + jeep).
The Chinnar–Marayoor road — dry-forest sanctuary, sandalwood, and the megalithic dolmens above Marayoor.
The Anachal glass bridge — and, more to the point, the estate road below it.
Bodimettu ghat — Munnar's quiet eastern exit, hairpins through shola forest to the plains with almost no tourist traffic.

offroad.summary: Tarmac throughout, but three of the legs are narrow forest or estate roads where surface and wildlife matter more than speed. Any bike handles it; an ADV is more comfortable on the broken Nelliyampathy and Marayoor stretches.
notes: Nelliyampathy ghat: narrow, with monsoon-broken edges and no railings at the falls. No fuel or food on the hill — Nenmara is the last.
Chinnar sanctuary road: single lane, elephants and gaur; check post allows daytime only. Don't stop for photos where there's no shoulder.
Anachal estate road: steep enough that the reel's commenters 'smell clutch plates' — first gear, and check the brakes before the descent.
Bodimettu ghat: cold and foggy early morning; the Tamil Nadu side has broken patches and truck traffic near Bodi.
Leech socks in the bag if any of it is within a month of the monsoon.

timings: Pothundi dam: 8 AM – 6 PM, ₹10. Kaikatty Forest IB (jeep tracks, Mampara): 7 AM – 3 PM; ₹50 forest entry, jeeps ₹1,200–2,000.
Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary road (Udumalpet–Marayoor): daytime crossing only; check-post timings roughly 6 AM – 6 PM.
Anachal glass bridge reopened July 2026 after a court order; hours and price change — check before relying on it.
Fuel: Coimbatore, Palakkad, Nenmara, Pollachi, Udumalpet, Marayoor, Munnar, Bodinayakanur, Theni. Fill at Nenmara and at Udumalpet.
Stays: Coimbatore (night 1), Pollachi or Nelliyampathy estate bungalows (night 2), Munnar (night 3).
cautions: Nelliyampathy is best avoided Jun–Aug (landslides, closed jeep tracks). Munnar is fine in monsoon but the Anachal road isn't.
The glass bridge was built on disputed land and closed once already — treat it as a bonus, not the reason for the trip.
Wild elephants: Chinnar, the Marayoor–Munnar road at dusk, and the Bodimettu ghat. Give way, engine off.
Four long days; the Bangalore–Coimbatore and Dindigul–Bangalore legs are 365 and 425 km of highway — don't stack them with the hill days.
